fact: A BCEAO decision published on 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions of the WAEMU to complete connection to PI-SPI and open services to the public.
The BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the union in April 2026 to be connected to PI-SPI and serving customers by 30 June 2026.
On 25 June 2026 the BCEAO moved the connection deadline for banks, e-money issuers and payment institutions to 30 September 2026, and gave microfinance institutions until 30 June 2027.

The UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report, as relayed by Horonya Finance, counts one licensed e-money issuer (EME) in Burkina Faso at end-2025, among 18 in the Union, and says Burkina Faso's EMEs hold 25.9% of e-money issued; the document gives no date for the licence, so the date is the end of 2025.

A BCEAO communiqué of 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions in the UEMOA to connect to the PI-SPI instant payment platform (30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions); Burkina Faso is a UEMOA member and had 13 authorised institutions on the platform at 31 July 2026, per Finance SAO.
L'Oeil du Sahel reports that the BCEAO's 2 October 2026 communique, covering Burkina Faso as a UEMOA state, sets binding rules for interoperable e-money transfers from 2 November 2026.
L'Oeil du Sahel reports that the BCEAO communique requires interoperable e-money transfers in UEMOA, including Burkina Faso, to be routed through PI-SPI from 2 November 2026.
L'Oeil du Sahel cites the UMOA banking commission as recording Orange Money Burkina Faso with 1.210 billion FCFA of capital and 314.818 billion FCFA of e-money outstanding at end 2024.
